sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Of the 10 species of Glyptotermes with known soldiers in South America, the soldier of this species is closest to G. guianensis in head width, but the frontal horn of the latter is angular in lateral view, whereas the frontal horn of this species is rounded; the frontal horn is the diagnostic character of the soldier of this species.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Dealated individual: head and pronotum chestnut brown (almost black in life); postclypeus transparent, labrum pale orange-brown; the wing scale of the fore wing concolorous with the pronotum; femora slightly paler than the pronotum, tibiae concolorous with the labrum. In lateral view the vertex bears 20—24 moderately long, scattered setae. In dorsal view each lateral margin of the pronotum bears about 20 setae of various lengths; in lateral view the setae are arranged along the anterior and posterior margins, with few in the middle. Compound eye small, dark grey, occupying less than 1/3 of the distance from the vertex to the genal margin; oval, its margin at the antennal socket almost straight. Ocellus small, orange, oval, separated from the compound eye by about its narrow diameter. Antennal segment formula 2<3>4=5. Pronotum wider than long, about as wide as the head excluding the compound eyes; anterior and posterior margins slightly concave, the sides slightly convex. Arolia present. Measurements (n=4, mean/range): head length to the labral apex 1.38/1.35—1.44 mm, head length to the mandible base 0.64/0.54—0.79 mm, head width 1.15/1.11—1.19 mm, compound eye diameter 0.26/0.25—0.30 mm, lower eye margin distance 0.27/0.23—0.33 mm, ocellus length 0.1/0.09—0.11 mm, pronotum median length 0.62/0.58—0.65 mm, maximum length 0.71/0.70—0.74 mm and width 1.19/1.09—1.26 mm, hind tibia length 0.91/0.86—0.96 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: In lateral view the head grades from pale orange at the cervical margin to dark brown at the frontal horn (darker in life); mandibles concolorous with the frons. Head capsule subcubical, its width about equal to its height, distinctly narrowed in the anterior quarter. Pronotum more than 2 times as wide as long, widest in the anterior third; anterior margin weakly concave, the posterior margin almost without a median concavity. Setae of head and pronotum moderate to long in dorsal and ventral view; the hump at the mandible base bears about 4—5 short setae. In lateral view setae sparser and more numerous only on the postmentum. Mandibles robust, about 2/3 of the total head length; curved towards the apex in the anterior half, the hump at the basal quarter evenly rounded behind the outer blade. Tooth formula see Fig. 3. Frons bilobed, the lobe apices rounded in lateral view; the frontal groove between the lobes extends to the postclypeus. The angle between vertex and frons is about 75°; in lateral view the frontal surface bears a large, nodular frontal horn. Eye spot very pale. In ventral view the posterior margin of the postmentum slightly wider than the middle. Genal angle rounded in dorsal view, projecting slightly beyond the narrowest part of the head capsule. Antennae 11—12 segmented, formula 2>3<4<5. Femora inflated. Measurements (n=9, mean/range): head length to the mandible base 1.44/1.09—1.70 mm, head width 1.22/1.00—1.32 mm, head height 1.11/0.95—1.18 mm, left mandible length 1.04/0.88—1.14 mm, postmentum maximum width 0.38/0.35—0.40 mm, minimum width 0.29/0.26—0.33 mm and length 1.12/0.89—1.25 mm, pronotum median length 0.54/0.40—0.61 mm, maximum length 0.65/0.51—0.74 mm and width 1.19/0.91—1.32 mm, hind tibia length 0.72/0.61—0.79 mm.

note: Adapted from the new-species description in Scheffrahn (2021), original in English; the alate is described only from dealated individuals; figure numbers (Figs 2—3), the holotype locality and the distribution map are not translated.
